segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The religious leaders were circling Jesus, demanding he say plainly who he claimed to be.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Instead of backing down, he reached into their own scriptures — to a psalm where God calls mere men gods.

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His point was sharp: if scripture called men gods because God's word came to them, how could they condemn the one the Father set apart?

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That was his answer. The Father himself set him apart and sent him into the world. Saying I am the Son of God was not blasphemy — it was the plain truth they would not test.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was not making himself a second God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was showing them their own book exposed their logic.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He stood on the scriptures they claimed to love. Come know him as he truly is.
